units.translation: 530. νήχυτον ὕδωρ: the much-poured. For νη signifies both privation and intensity. And ‘ἀχύνετον ὕδωρ’ (Nic. Al. 174) means ‘much’ among the Ionians and Sicilians. Dionysius: ‘πλαζομέναις ἵνα λύσσαν ἀχύνετον ἧκα βαλοῦσα.’
18 sch. IV 1367 Hesych. νήχυτον Et. M. 602, 40 Eust. 163, 24
19 sch. Nic. Al. 174 Hesych. ἀχύνετον Et. M. 183, 7
19 ἀχύνετον ὕδωρ 〈τὸ πολύχυτον· καὶ ἀχύνετον〉 τὸ πολὺ proposed by K
20 about Dionysius it is not established; Lobeck Pathol. 1, 1853, 201 thought he was the first to recognize him as the author of the Bassarica
21 ἐνὶ instead of ἵνα Valckenaer Amm. 1739, anim. 148
533a. Stars and moon: he tells the traditional story, that sorceresses bring down the moon. Some also called the eclipses of the sun and moon ‘overthrowings’ of the gods. L
22 sch. IV 59/61 a. b Ar. Nub. 749 with sch. Luc. Philops. 14 Sen. Med. 790 sqq. Lucan. Phars. VI 499 sqq.

b. In ancient times they thought that sorceresses brought down the moon and the sun. Therefore even down to the time of Democritus (68 B 161 Diels-Kranz) many called eclipses ‘overthrowings’. Sosiphanes in Meleager (fg 1 N.²): ‘μάγοις ἐπῳδαῖς πᾶσα Θεσσαλὶς κόρη ψευδὴς σελήνης αἰθέρος καταιβάτις.’
11 sch. Lyc. 87 Corn. Theol. gr. comp. 24 (46, 9 L.) Or. Werf. 616, 2 Et. M. 664, 52
1 W separated sch. b from a; τὰς φ-ας W : αἱ φ-ες
2 Δημοκρίτου P : -κράτους L
5 Θεσσαλὶς P : πεσσ- L
6 perhaps καθαιρέτις
539a. τάχα is used for doubt; but some take it as equivalent to ταχέως. L
7 ἐπὶ K : ἐν
b. 〈σὺν δαίμονι:〉 with a good deity. Lg

550. 〈κείνης δ’ ὅτε μείλιχος ὄρνις:〉 Apollodorus says in his work On the Gods (244 fg 114 J.) that the dove is sacred to Aphrodite because of its lecherousness; for it is so called from ‘loving excessively’.
11 Hefermehl Studia in Ap. π. θ. fragm. Genev., Diss. Berol. 1905, 39 thinks that the number of the book has been lost after ἐν τῷ
12 διὰ τὸ Heyne Apoll. Bibl.² 1803, 396 : διὸ καὶ λάγνον L : -η. καὶ τὸ ὄνομα δηλοῖ P
551-52. κέαρ δέ μοι: but as my soul foresees, so may it happen. L
561. 〈βλέποντες:〉 it is written λεύσσοντες. Gg
15 βλέποντες, which was formerly a gloss, is found in G as the poet's word. cf. W 52
564. 〈μεμαώς:〉 equivalent to ‘being angry’ here; for no one is eager for evils. Lm
578. 〈Μινύαισι:〉 to the Argonauts. Lg
581. 〈λασίης:〉 thick. Lg
583a. ἀποφλύξωσιν: equivalent to ἐκφυσήσωσιν, but it ends up meaning ἐκπνεύσωσιν. Hence also φλύαρος.
b. 〈ἀποφλύξωσιν:〉 they will give back. Sm
584. 〈οὐδὲ γάρ:〉 the word ὑπέμεινεν is missing. Lm
